stem: One root module holds networking, a database tier and 40 application services. Every plan takes 25 minutes and a typo in a service change once put the database in the same plan. Which restructuring best addresses both problems?

Convert the services to CLI workspaces inside the same directory so that each service gets a separate state file under the one backend
Split it into configurations along ownership and change-frequency lines, each with its own state, sharing values via outputs
Raise -parallelism to a much higher value so the graph walk finishes sooner, and keep a single state for easier cross-references

stem: A network configuration exposes its VPC ID as a root output, and an application configuration in another state reads it with a terraform_remote_state data source. A security reviewer objects. Which concern is accurate?

choices.text: The data source copies the network outputs into the application state, so any later change to the output is never seen by the consumer

stem: A team uses CLI workspaces named dev and prod with one S3 backend. Auditors find that engineers with dev credentials can run terraform workspace select prod and apply. What is the underlying design flaw?

choices.text: CLI workspaces within a directory share one backend and its credentials, so they do not provide access separation between environments
The default workspace is always mapped to production, and selecting any other workspace therefore inherits its permissions
The prod workspace was created with terraform workspace new, which grants every user of the backend write access to it by default

stem: A shared VPC was created in the monolith state, and it must move to a new network configuration without destroying it. Which sequence achieves this?

choices.text: Add replace_triggered_by in the new configuration, which transfers the VPC object from the old state during the next plan
Add an import block in the new configuration for the VPC, apply it, then drop the object from the old state without destroying it

stem: Which TWO situations justify splitting a Terraform project into separate configurations with separate states? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A module call is repeated three times, so each repetition must be stored in its own state to keep names unique
Two engineers want to avoid editing the same file, so the project is divided into a main.tf and a network.tf per person

stem: An instance is healthy in the console but its disk is corrupted and the team wants a fresh one with the same configuration. Which command plans exactly that without changing the code?

stem: Someone resized a managed database in the console. The team wants Terraform state to record the new size, but must not change any infrastructure yet. Which command and result fit?

terraform apply -target=aws_db_instance.main, which sets the state size and leaves the database unchanged
